origin: Original Cloudbath production directions. No upstream STYLE.md text is included or loaded by this library.
renderer_dependency: Lemo core/lib.js, MIT, pinned in upstream.lock.json

styles.dataviz: Make the explanation visible through the actual objects in the narration. Establish one question, show a meaningful comparison or a concrete mechanism, then resolve it. Numeric charts require numbers explicitly supplied in the verified story data; when a quantity is unknown, show the uncertainty instead of drawing an invented distribution. Move the represented objects as the explanation changes, keeping scale, grouping and labels consistent. Use a small number of large Thai labels, ample spacing and clear foreground/background separation. Animation should reveal relationships, not merely count or decorate text.
styles.firefly-pointillism: Build a coherent scene from the story's named subjects, setting and actions. Use small luminous points as a supporting technique: they can trace a path, gather around an explained mechanism or connect successive states. Keep the important subject recognizable in every frame and distinguish imaginative illustration from evidence. Preserve the same palette and lighting direction across scenes. Guide attention with restrained movement and camera changes tied to the narration; particles must not obscure the subject or become a substitute for explaining it.
styles.rubber-hose: Create original expressive characters appropriate to this story, with consistent silhouettes, clothing and props. Communicate each beat through an understandable action and reaction: anticipation, action, then a held expression or consequence. Flexible limbs and modest squash/stretch may strengthen the action while faces and identities remain recognizable. Stage the characters in a clear environment with the specific objects mentioned by the narrator. Keep the comic timing readable and avoid constant bouncing without purpose. Do not copy a known mascot, branded character or upstream demo. A story without people or animals may use expressive objects instead.
